subject.title: Bound historical public repository proof reuse after expiry

question: Should the historical outage fallback remain strictly fail-closed at proof expiry, or may it accept a narrowly bounded post-expiry interval such as the five seconds proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/octopool/pull/31?
rationale: The reported condition concerns authorization evidence after its expiry. Choosing a grace period changes the repository's security/availability tradeoff and cannot be inferred safely from the closed unmerged PR.

options.title: Require strict expiry
options.body: Reject historical proofs once `expires_at` has passed, preserving the strongest authorization boundary at the cost of more outage-time failures.

options.title: Approve a bounded grace
options.body: Permit a specifically documented short interval only if runtime validation and the authoritative D1 query enforce the same limit with focused regression tests.

recommendation.title: Require strict expiry
recommendation.body: Reject historical proofs once `expires_at` has passed, preserving the strongest authorization boundary at the cost of more outage-time failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged public-proof fallback work makes this person the strongest available history-based owner for the security-policy decision.
